statement: You are given an array hand of card values and an integer groupSize. Decide whether the cards can be split into groups so that every card is in exactly one group, every group has exactly groupSize cards, and the values in each group are consecutive.
Return true if such a split exists and false otherwise.

A greedy method works: the smallest card left must start a group, so take it together with the next groupSize − 1 consecutive values, and fail if any of them is missing. A min-heap or ordered map of card counts makes the smallest card easy to find. If hand.length is not a multiple of groupSize the answer is false straight away.

examples.explanation: 5 cards cannot be divided into groups of 4.
6 cards could make two groups of 3, but the group starting at the smallest card, 1, needs a 3, and there is none.
